changes: p1 name normalized to 'Vidyāraṇya' (muni kept as title only); his role is author only

p2 Bhāratītīrtha: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. He is the commentator's guru, not a teacher connected with the production of this copy. 'munivarya' and 'paramahaṃsaparivrājakācārya' qualify both gurus in the compound
p3 Rāmakṛṣṇa: title 'vidvas' removed ('viduṣā' is descriptive, not a title)
Relations kept: Rāmakṛṣṇa pupil_of Bhāratītīrtha and of Vidyāraṇya (the compound '-śiṣyeṇa' covers both)

Date: pakṣa normalized to śukla ('dale … dhava[le]'); the possible meaning of lakṣmījānidina as ekādaśī/harivāsara is noted; era kept as ŚS on the basis of 'śaka[re]', confidence low; the year can't be computed

date.as_written: aṅkendudakadairmete (!) śakara ite patyaudyutīnāṃ ghane lakṣmījānidine dale tu dhava lekhīḥ

notes: The date verse is badly corrupt. 'aṅkendudakadairmete' is a bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram, perhaps aṅka(9)-indu(1)-…-mite. The middle number-words can't be recovered, so no year is given. 'śakara ite' probably stands for 'śake' (+ something), so the era is tentatively ŚS. 'patyau dyutīnāṃ ghane' probably names the sun (dyutipati) in some rāśi, but the month can't be identified with certainty. 'lakṣmījānidine' = 'on Viṣṇu's day', which could mean ekādaśī or a weekday. 'lekhīḥ' = 'wrote', but the scribe is not named. 'aglovīvīt (!)' is unintelligible. 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇa śrīrāmakṛṣṇagopāla' at the end looks like a devotional invocation. It could also be the scribe's signature, but no scribe is recorded here. Bhāratītīrtha and Vidyāraṇya are named only as the commentator's gurus. The catalogue fields are empty.
